title: Keep credentials private
summary: Some real APIs need credentials. Use the tool's appropriate local or secret storage and authorised access; do not copy real tokens into examples or public collections.
introduction: Some real APIs need credentials. Use the tool's appropriate local or secret storage and authorised access; do not copy real tokens into examples or public collections. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.title: Keep credentials private

blocks.text: The request documentation can be shared without publishing the secret. Postman cloud sync and collaboration have their own privacy settings.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Identify which parts of an example are safe to share.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Removing a token from a new export does not revoke a token that was already leaked.
For more detail later, use this [Postman further reading](https://learning.postman.com/docs/getting-started/overview/).
